choices: The Department of Health and Human Services
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
The Federal Emergency Management Agency
The Department of Transportation
questions.explanation: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is the federal source for the model EMT scope of practice and the national education standards.
questions.question: You're teaching a National Registry review course, and a student asks where the model EMT scope of practice and the national EMT education standards come from at the federal level. What do you tell her?

choices: The Ryan White Act
The Marchman Act
The Equal Rights Amendment
The Americans with Disabilities Act
questions.explanation: The Americans with Disabilities Act is the legislation that protects people with disabilities from being denied access to programs and services provided by state or local governments.
questions.question: Another student in your class, who uses a wheelchair, asks which federal law protects people with disabilities from being denied access to programs and services run by state or local governments. Which law is she asking about?

choices: Comprehensive, quality, evidence-based care that is convenient and efficient, with preventive care and patient records that are easy to access
A system judged mainly by response times and the number of patients transported
Care that starts only once a patient reaches the hospital, with records kept inside each agency
Emergency care only, with prevention left entirely to public health departments
questions.explanation: EMS Agenda 2050 describes people-centered care as comprehensive, quality, convenient, evidence-based, and efficient, and it adds preventive care plus comprehensive, easily accessible patient records.
questions.question: Your agency is rebuilding its system around the EMS Agenda 2050 vision of a people-centered EMS system. Which description best matches that vision?

choices: Provide appropriate medical care
Diagnose the patient's condition
Ensure your own personal safety
Provide transport to the closest hospital
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes before everything else on a call — an EMT who gets hurt can't help the patient, so safety outranks care, diagnosis, and transport.
questions.question: You're a brand-new EMT pulling into the driveway on your first cardiac arrest, with a police car and a firefighter's truck already on scene. Before any patient care happens, what has to come first?

choices: Performing a patient assessment
Providing legal advice to patients
Protecting patient privacy and confidentiality
Upholding medical and legal standards
questions.explanation: An EMT's responsibilities include being prepared for the call, patient assessment and care, scene safety, privacy, and upholding medical and legal standards — but giving patients legal advice is not among them.
questions.question: All of the following are part of an EMT's roles and responsibilities EXCEPT:

choices: Assess the patient's current status — consciousness, airway, breathing, and oxygen needs — while monitoring vital signs and staying ready to resume CPR
Move straight to packaging and transport without reassessing, since the pulse is back
Leave the patient's side to search the house for his medication bottles
Call in a full report to the hospital before touching the patient
questions.explanation: A returning pulse doesn't end the emergency: reassess the patient's status and vital signs, support the airway and breathing as needed, and be prepared to resume CPR if he arrests again. Looking for scene clues about history and medications comes after that.
questions.question: On your first arrest, the police officer started CPR and the firefighter's AED shock brought back a carotid pulse before you walked in. Working alongside your paramedic partner, what should your immediate focus be?

choices: Once the patient is packaged, no further assessment is needed until you arrive
Checking the patient once, halfway there, to limit distractions
Saving all treatments until the hospital so nothing is done wrong en route
Reassessing frequently — vital signs and patient status — and checking that ongoing treatments are working and given correctly
questions.explanation: Transport isn't a pause in care: frequent reassessment catches changes in the patient's status, and ongoing treatments have to be monitored for effectiveness and correct administration the whole way.
questions.question: The firefighter drives so you and your partner can both work in the back during the ride to the hospital. What does successful patient management during this transport look like?

choices: Teaching EMS courses
Pursuing an advanced degree
Continuing medical education
Completing weekly drug screening
questions.explanation: Continuing medical education is the continuous phase — it goes on for as long as you practice, unlike a degree or a teaching role that starts and ends.
questions.question: A student asks which phase of being an emergency health care provider never really stops — the one that runs continuously for an entire career. What is it?

choices: Projecting a sense of personal superiority so the team follows your lead
Communicating clearly while treating the people you speak to with respect
Keeping every task for yourself so nothing gets missed
Assuming the other responders' work doesn't need your attention
questions.explanation: Teamwork and diplomacy come down to being able to communicate while giving respect to the listener — that's what lets different agencies function as one team.
questions.question: Four different responders — a police officer, a firefighter, you, and your paramedic partner — are all working the same cardiac arrest. Which behavior best demonstrates teamwork and diplomacy?

choices: Honest behavior, a clean and well-groomed appearance, and respect for others
Integrity, but relying only on yourself and taking charge of every scene
Putting your own needs first while still listening to the patient
Blaming others when a call goes badly and ignoring team members
questions.explanation: Professional attributes include honest behavior, a clean and well-groomed persona, and respecting others — blaming others, lying, and ignoring team members are the opposite of professional.
questions.question: Which set of traits best describes the professional attributes expected of an EMT?

choices: Explain everything in full medical terminology so she understands how serious this is
Promise her that her father is going to recover so she calms down
Be honest and empathetic — explain in plain language what you're doing for her father, without speculating about how he'll do
Tell her confidentiality rules mean you can't say anything, and have her wait outside
questions.explanation: Family members need truthful, professional, empathetic communication in plain language — no technical jargon or euphemisms, and no speculation about the patient's current or future status, while still respecting confidentiality.
questions.question: Mid-arrest, the patient's daughter arrives, confused and very upset. She told her father to rest while she called 9-1-1, and now she's watching you work on him. What's the best way to handle her?

choices: Managing a patient in cardiac arrest
Administering vaccines to prevent disease
Teaching safety in schools before any injury has happened
Teaching pool safety to the people at the scene after treating a man who slipped and fell by the pool
questions.explanation: The pool-safety teaching happens after an injury, aimed at the people involved so it doesn't happen again — that's secondary prevention. Vaccines and school safety lessons come before any injury, which makes them primary prevention.
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of secondary prevention?

choices: It disciplines the EMTs involved so the problem doesn't happen again
It reviews and audits all aspects of the EMS system to find what needs improvement, then fixes problems through remediation and training
It looks only at the single call where the problem was first noticed
It sends the problem to the state EMS office and waits for a ruling
questions.explanation: CQI is a circular system of continuous internal and external reviews and audits of all aspects of an EMS system; it identifies areas that need improvement and resolves them through remediation and training rather than punitive measures.
questions.question: Your agency's run reviews keep turning up the same documentation problem, and the CQI process takes it on. How does continuous quality improvement approach a problem like this?

choices: Research generates the data that show which treatments are actually beneficial or lifesaving — and which are not — so patient care can keep improving
Research matters only for physicians; EMTs just follow orders
Once a treatment is in the protocols, research on it is finished
Research exists mainly to publish papers, not to change field care
questions.explanation: Research provides data that identify which treatments are beneficial or lifesaving for patients and which are not, and participating in EMS research lets the EMT help shape the future of care.
questions.question: A student shrugs and says crews already know what works, so why does EMS need research at all? What's the best answer?
